# AAIF alignment design review

Review date: 2026-10-23. Baseline: `2fc2fe7`; reviewed the uncommitted docs-only strategy. This review records design findings, not runtime qualification or approval of an integration.

## Findings

**F1 — High: AF-4 couples independent profiles into one gate.** [The work order](../../../plans/aaif-alignment.md) line 35 gives AF-4 hard `needs: "AF-1, AF-2, AF-3"`, while [G15](../../../intent/scope.md) line 19 asks for one controlled workflow across two independently implemented supported peers/hosts. A named consumer could prove the pinned MCP tool boundary through two independent hosts without using Open Responses; the current dependency still blocks AF-4 on AF-2. Conversely, a Responses comparison need not wait for a goose pilot. Lines 37-39 narrow feature scope but do not remove the graph dependency. Make AF-4 depend on one explicitly chosen applicable profile and its independent expected-case set, with AF-1/2/3 as conditional evidence links. Preserve separate qualifications and require the G15 task to state its exact common interface and which two implementations were observed. This also keeps the two-slot ceiling and W1-W4 order intact.

**F2 — Medium: sandbox escape wording exceeds a falsifiable acceptance claim.** [AF-A07](../../../designs/aaif-alignment.md) line 188 says a real runtime "denies the planted escape/egress cases," while lines 133-140 correctly require selected-network probes and distinguish mocked translation from backend proof. A finite planted test can establish that *specified* escape attempts failed under a pinned runtime/configuration; it cannot establish containment against the class of escapes or certify OpenSandbox security. The [pinned OpenSandbox egress specification](https://github.com/opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox/blob/f3f4a7f419e526de4c3deb250d72fc034986fc28/specs/egress-api.yaml) explicitly warns that a `503` does not prove packet isolation or rollback. State the threat assumptions, exact attacks, network destinations, observed effects and residual unknowns. Use “specified isolation-boundary and egress probes failed to cross the boundary” as the acceptance outcome, and do not generalize beyond that profile.

**F3 — Medium: G15 comparison can pass without one shared capability.** [G15](../../../intent/scope.md) line 19 and [AF-A14](../../../designs/aaif-alignment.md) line 195 require two independently implemented peers/hosts and comparable outcomes/cost, but neither explicitly requires both to exercise the *same required task and selected interface/profile*. For example, a Codex Agent Skills loading test and an MCP goose tool test could be counted as two hosts while testing different contracts. Bind the denominator and required negative cases to one versioned task/profile before choosing peers; report unsupported cases per peer. A narrow profile can pass while the broader ten-project assessment remains a map, not a compliance claim.

## Verified scope and boundaries

The [Linux Foundation announcement](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/agentic-ai-foundation-announces-four-new-projects-agent-skills-open-responses-openenv-and-opensandbox) names the four 2026-10-22 additions, and the [AAIF directory](https://aaif.io/projects) lists all ten covered in the [assessment](../../../assessments/2026-10-23-aaif-alignment.md) lines 26-37. The [Open Responses specification](https://www.openresponses.org/specification) shows the cited 2026-04-24 revision; the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) supports folder/name validation and labels `allowed-tools` experimental. The assessment distinguishes upstream source, existing `UseResponses`, conditional plans and unverified runtime behavior. I found no adoption or affiliation claim in the reviewed text.

The proposed optional profiles preserve I1, I18 and I20 as stated, leave [0003](../../../intent/decisions/0003-mcp-revisions-track-never-chase.md)'s MCP revision trigger un-fired, retain [0024](../../../intent/decisions/0024-independent-kits-share-identity-not-authority.md)'s domain authority, and keep [0032/0033](../../../intent/decisions/0032-admit-offline-practice-review-and-local-diagnostics.md)'s second slot. No accepted non-goal or future promotion is implied by the announcement. Raw Fathom O11 obligations are incomplete and were not treated as assurance. `review_diff` on the docs returned an indexed, partly stale impact receipt, not a design verdict. No code, host, provider, sandbox or external peer was executed in this review.

## Follow-up disposition

Rechecked the revised docs on 2026-10-23. **F1 addressed:** [AF-4](../../../plans/aaif-alignment.md) is deferred until a receiver selects a common interface, then requires only the applicable AF-1/2/3 qualifications. Its eventual `needs:` are authored at admission; no all-three dependency remains. **F2 addressed:** [AF-C08 and AF-A07](../../../designs/aaif-alignment.md) now bind real probes to a declared threat model, backend and configuration, retain untested escape classes and residual unknowns, and disclaim security certification. **F3 addressed:** [G15](../../../intent/scope.md) and AF-A14 require the same controlled task and interface profile; AF-A14 also binds the input snapshot and policy floors across independent real implementations/hosts.

[0034](../../../intent/decisions/0034-open-ecosystem-interoperability.md) now separately defers submitting the kit for AAIF hosting until D4 is ratified and a proposal's fit is reviewed. That preserves the public-readiness boundary while allowing project-level interoperability and contribution work. These edits resolve the three design findings; no implementation or runtime claim follows. Root owns final validation and any later admission decision.
